entertainment.title: 5 Best Moments of the 2026 HEAT Latin Music Awards: Olga Tañón, Gloria Trevi & More
entertainment.summary: The gala, which took place in Mexico for the first time, was held on Thursday (Nov. 5) in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco.
entertainment.body:
The HEAT Latin Music Awards, popularly known as Premios HEAT, were held for the first time in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico, on Thursday (Nov. 5). The ceremony attracted a slew of stars, including Gloria Trevi, Olga Tañón, Los Ángeles Azules, Jessi Uribe, Arthur Hanlon, La Arrolladora Banda El Limón de René Camacho and Piso 21.

The event, which took place at the Puerto Vallarta International Convention Center and was broadcast live on LosHeat.tv and Jalisco TV, celebrated a variety of genres, including regional Mexican music, pop, urbano, cumbia, reparto and reggaetón. Joining the event were artists such as Ha*Ash, Majo Aguilar, Mar Solís, Dayanara, Paola Jara, Pututi & Nesty, Grupo 5 and Corridos Del Rey.

One standout performances of the evening was a segment titled “Los que siempre viven” (“Those Who Live On”), where various artists sang timeless classics in tribute to late legends such as Selena, Vicente Fernández, José José, Paquita la del Barrio, Antonio Aguilar and Flor Silvestre, creating an emotional and heartfelt moment.

Another highlight was the tribute to Puerto Rican merengue icon Olga Tañón’s career. Also known as “La Mujer de Fuego” (Woman of Fire), Tañon shared the stage with Mar Solís and Grupo 5, performing “Contigo o Sin Ti” with the former and the classic “Ya Me Cansé” with the latter.

The Mexican-American sister duo Ha*Ash delivered a live performance of its new single “Antes Que Te Cases,” originally recorded with Cristian Castro, taking its pop music to new heights. Meanwhile, Gloria Trevi, who was honored this year as Artista Oro (Golden Artist) at the HEAT Latin Music Awards al Estilo Jalisco, closed the show with a vibrant medley of her greatest hits, including “Todos Me Miran,” “Me Lloras,” “Pelo Suelto” and “Con Los Ojos Cerrados.”

Here are five standout moments from the HEAT Latin Music Awards al Estilo Jalisco, organized in collaboration with the government of Jalisco and the municipality of Puerto Vallarta, in alphabetical order of the artists involved.

The masterful piano of composer and arranger Arthur Hanlon joined forces with the impeccable vocals of Colombian popular music singer Jessi Uribe for a version of “Si Ya Me Voy” — a song also recorded in a banda style alongside Luis Ángel “El Flaco.” The fusion of Uribe’s traditional sound with the jazz and Motown influences rooted in Hanlon’s native Detroit resulted in a flawless blend of classical virtuosity and Latin rhythms.

entertainment.title: Taylor Swift Called the ‘Fakest’ New York Knicks Fan by 2 of Team’s Players: ‘It’s a Little Performative’
entertainment.summary: "I'm gonna get some hate from the Swifties," Tyler Kolek acknowledged.
entertainment.body:
After drawing ire from disgruntled football fans in 2023 who felt she was present at too many games, Taylor Swift has managed to irk men in another sport for apparently attending too few. New York Knicks point guards Tyler Kolek and Miles “Deuce” McBride recently criticized the pop star as the “fakest” fan of the 2026 NBA champions, accusing her and other celebrity row visitors of being “performative.”

In a clip from an NBA 2K TikTok livestream Deflected posted Thursday (Nov. 5), the two men fiddled with game controllers while debating who they believe is the least authentic celebrity Knicks fan. “Maybe Taylor Swift,” Kolek said, to which McBride offered, “I would agree.”

What defines a “fake” Knicks fan, in their eyes? “They just want to be seen at the game, they’re not necessarily fans,” Kolek noted. “I don’t know if I’ve seen her at any other games. I’m gonna get some hate from the Swifties. I guess she’s got a lot going on, so she can’t come all the time. But it’s a little performative.”

“Swifties not gonna like that answer,” McBride said with a laugh as the two players shouted out Ben Stiller and Tracy Morgan for showing up consistently at Knicks games. “Everybody else [but Swift] is usually solid.”

In a statement, a spokesperson for the Knicks told Billboard , “Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization.”

The 14-time Grammy winner was present at Game 4 of the NBA Finals, cheering on the Knicks alongside Mariska Hargitay and Este and Alana Haim in custom Knicks T-shirts. Before that, she also traveled with now-husband Travis Kelce to watch an away game against the Cleveland Cavaliers.

It’s ironic that Swift — who, as Kolek generously pointed out, might’ve been a little busy this season, having been gearing up to release Billboard Hot 100 -topping song “I Knew It, I Knew You” for Toy Story 5 the same month of the NBA Finals, among other projects — is now getting flack for this reason. It wasn’t long ago that football fans expressed upset over the amount that she was seen at NFL games when she first started showing up to support Kelce.

“I think we all know that if there’s one thing that male sports fans want to see in their spaces and on their screens,” Swift later sarcastically joked about the outrage in her 2025 cameo on New Heights , “it’s more of me.”

entertainment.title: Lil Baby’s ‘FRESH’: All 17 Tracks Ranked
entertainment.summary: See how Billboard ranks the new songs from Lil Baby's new album, FRESH .
entertainment.body:
Lil Baby finds himself at an interesting point in his career. On one hand, he’s six years removed from his star-making My Turn era, and hasn’t had the same kind of hit records or released a critically acclaimed album since. Conversely, he has also amassed 160 Billboard Hot 100 entries (including 13 top 10s) throughout his career, as well as four consecutive Billboard 200 No. 1 albums, showing that his core audience and beyond have remained invested in what he puts out.

In the music game, though, narratives are often just as impactful as numbers. So while one person may feel he is still highly successful, another may rightfully say he has lost steam since the massive “We Paid” with 42 Dugg, and his politically-charged anthem “The Bigger Picture.”

As for Baby himself — per his recent comments on Popcast — he doesn’t even view what could be perceived as a “cold streak” as a slump. This year’s “Dead Fresh”, a top 20 song on the Billboard Hot 100, showed some people that even if he can’t catch lightning in a bottle again, he still has a little electricity in his arsenal. The true intrigue, for many, is: How can he evolve his style? What new stories does he have to tell? Was 2020-2022 just a run, or is he as good as he established himself then to be?

His new album FRESH isn’t a major shift in his sound, and doesn’t reveal much new about him. But it is a reminder that he can rap well, and is among the best of this era within his tier of artists. There are some fun, inspired production choices, but, for the most part, Lil Baby remains who we have always known him to be. Check out our ranked list of the 17 tracks on FRESH below.

entertainment.title: Meet the British Foodie Demystifying the Michelin Guide’s Secrets
entertainment.summary: Jesse Burgess courted a devout following with his intimate access to London restaurant luminaries; now he's the Gordon Ramsay-approved face of Apple TV's 'Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars.'
entertainment.body:
Jesse Burgess is a chef whisperer. If you’re interested in food and have a penchant for scrolling, you may already know this from one of his many vertical clips.

The 35-year-old English foodie, host and co-founder of media platform TopJaw, forged a reputation for charming London’s culinary luminaries into opening up not just about their work but the restaurants, bars and Sunday roasts that they adore. And, just as informative, the spots that they think are overrated.

Interviewing chef after chef after chef for going on 10 years, Burgess has honed another rather novel skill. He can talk about fine dining without a ring of pretension. “This guy properly reads the fucking room,” says Gordon Ramsay , several times a TopJaw guest. “Jesse understands what he does and doesn’t know. He talks from a viewer’s perspective and lets you in on the secret, what’s going on … where a critic would have the tendency to slide toward being an asshole.” Related Stories TV Apple TV Renews 'Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars' for Season 3 TV Toni Collette to Lead Apple TV Dramedy 'Lenni'

An asshole was the last thing Apple TV needed when casting its ambitious culinary series, Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars . The word Michelin already evokes thoughts of white tablecloths, comical price tags, foams, fermentations and microgreens applied via tweezers. (And, you know, the whole tire manufacturing part of the business.) To preemptively deflate perceived elitism, many associated with the project say there was ultimately only one choice to be its face.

“I’d heard about the show, because they had already filmed quite a bit of it without a host, flying to chefs all around the world,” says Burgess, over lunch this past summer in East Hollywood. “I didn’t think I had a hope in hell of getting the job.”

The series was being produced by Studio Ramsay Global, so it was Ramsay who suggested Burgess fly out to do a screen test during the first season’s Sweden shoot. “We had a long list of A-listers lining up to present the show, and Apple wanted some of their own talent, but Jesse, from my side, was the running favorite from day one,” says Ramsay. “What makes him special is his vulnerability in these situations”

It’s a unique situation in which Burgess found himself. Ostensibly another cooking competition, Knife Edge , which concludes its second season on Nov. 6, follows chefs from around the world as they strive to earn, maintain or up their count of stars in the storied Michelin guide. They punch walls. They weep. They hemorrhage money. They make very appetizing meals. But in lieu of having Burgess exhaustively interview them, he’s almost the translator of their work — narrating the trials of operating a restaurant and describing meals as he eats them with the relatable manner of a thoughtful guy at the pub who just really wants to tell you about his burger.

entertainment.title: Why Tom Petty ‘Origins 1971-1978’ Isn’t Your Normal Box Set: ‘The Important Thing Was Making a Good Album’
entertainment.summary: The set of rarities rounds up Tom Petty & the Heartbreaker's "feral" early recordings from the '70s.
entertainment.body:
Adria Petty says an anniversary, to her, is “a very uncool marketing thing.” But this year’s 50th anniversary of the self-titled debut album by her father, the late Tom Petty, and his band the Heartbreakers was too good of a storytelling opportunity to pass up. Explore Tom Petty & the Heartbreakers See latest videos, charts and news

“I really want to acknowledge the Heartbreakers this year, ’cause they’re all alive and have achieved so much and are still going strong now,” Petty — who co-produced the new box set Origins 1971-78 — tells Billboard via Zoom from California. “This anniversary is really important to us. It’s really important to us that everybody gets their flowers when they’re still alive…. ( Origins ) is the musical diagram to how Tom became Tom and the Heartbreakers and how they found their way to this music.” Related Queens of the Stone Age Crowned on ARIA Chart With 'Perfecth' Lil Baby Brings 'Fresh' to Life: Stream It Now Lil Baby, JENNIE, Dove Cameron, XG, Boys Noize & More: New Music Friday Guide

Out Friday (Nov. 6), Origins represents a two-year undertaking that dove deep into Petty and the Heartbreakers’ vaults, primarily conducted by the Petty Legacy LLC brain trust which also includes longtime producer/engineer Ryan Ulyate and managers Will Botwin and Scott Greer. The multi-disc set includes new mixes of Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers and 1978’s You’re Gonna Get It! (with extended versions of some of the tracks), an unreleased Live From the Record Plant 1977 performance and videos from the BBC’s Old Grey Whistle Test in 1978.

The focal point, however, is No Sleep Til L.A ., which features a dozen early tracks from 1971-77 — recorded by the pre-Heartbreakers band Mudcrutch and Petty solo in addition to the Heartbreakers — as well as five more included on an EP dubbed The Cut Out Bin . Those will also be issued as a separate, individual album as well as on the box set.

“This body of work, to me, is sort of a Rosetta Stone for rock ‘n’ roll in a weird way,” explains Adria Petty, a music video and commercial director in addition to her Petty Legacy role. Since Tom Petty’s death in 2017 at the age of 66, she’s also co-produced archival projects. “They could take it to reggae, they could take it to disco, they could take it to soul, they could really take it to country rock — this, that or the other. They went their own way and became an amalgam of all that. They were just experimenting, making noise together that they liked. My responsibility here is to point out the cultural importance, that during disco, during their aftermath of Vietnam, these guys blazed their own trail and kept it going for 50 years.”

entertainment.title: Melania Trump Dismisses Media as “Noise” in Trailer for ‘Melania’ Doc Follow-Up
entertainment.summary: Prime Video's two-part series featuring footage not included in the film about the first lady released earlier this year.
entertainment.body:
Melania Trump isn’t especially impressed by her media coverage in the trailer for Melania, the two-part docuseries from Prime Video about the first lady that dropped on Friday ahead of a Nov. 20 premiere.

“The media, they want gossip. For me, it’s noise,” Melania Trump says in the teaser for the two-parter follow-up to the Melania documentary released earlier this year , made from bonus footage shot by director Brett Ratner as his cameras followed her in the days after President Donald Trump ‘s second inauguration. Of course, Melania Trump got more serious press coverage after she recently brokered a local and six-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the occupied city of Oleshky. Related Stories TV Prime Video's 'Terminal List' Franchise Expands With 'Savage Son' Series TV 'Off Campus' Season 2 Sets April Premiere Date

But the docuseries will focus on Melania Trump as a wife and mother, especially to son Barron Trump, who she insists in the trailer is her priority. “The honor of serving as first lady comes with an immediate call to action. Moments after the inauguration, first lady Melania Trump sets her mission in motion for the American people,” a synopsis from the producers states about the second episode, entitled Pride & Honor.

Prime Video will stream Melania worldwide after the earlier theatrical release of Melania , the movie, which grossed around $16.6 million at the box office. Amazon ’s $75 million deal for Melania included two additional episodes of bonus footage not included in the theatrical documentary that also streamed on Prime Video.

Melania the follow-up docuseries was produced by Amazon MGM Studios, Muse Films, New Element Media and RatPac Entertainment. Melania Trump and Marc Beckman executive produce the docuseries directed by Brett Ratner, who also produces along with Fernando Sulichin.

entertainment.title: 25th Anniversary Edition of Britney Spears’ Self-Titled Third LP Features 11 Bonus Tracks: Listen
entertainment.summary: Among the additions to the 2001 album are five songs being released for the first time.
entertainment.body:
Britney Spears ‘ third studio album, 2001’s Britney , was reissued in an expanded edition on Friday (Nov. 6) featuring the entire original album along with 11 bonus tracks. The digital version of the LP is available now, with a physical package due out on Jan. 22 available for pre-order now here .

The expanded edition also includes five songs that are being officially released for the first time: the 2022 Pepsi commercial track “Right Now (Taste The Victory),” “She’ll Never Be Me,” “Am I A Sinner,” “When I Say So” and “My Big Secret,” as well as two remixes, “Overprotected (Darkchild Remix),” and “Boys (feat. Pharrell Williams) (The Co-Ed Remix).”

The vinyl version of the album will be pressed on Bombastic Blue Splatter, with the package for the physical version including unreleased photos from the period when the singer recorded the LP, according to a press release. Another vinyl variant, a liquid-filled version from Bad World, is also available for pre-order today.

Britney was originally released on Nov. 6, 2001 and debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, cementing Spears’ place in music history as the first female artist ever to have their first three studio albums debut at No. 1. It spawned the Billboard Hot 100 No. 27 hit “I’m a Slave 4 U” and the Nov. 86 hit “Overprotected,” and featured the fan-favorite songs “I’m Not a Girl, Not Yet a Woman,” as well as “Boys,” and a cover of Joan Jett’s “I Love Rock ‘n’ Roll.” The original album ends with “What It’s Like to Be Me,” a track co-written and co-produced by Spears’ then boyfriend, *NSYNC’s Justin Timberlake, and choreographer Wade Robson.

Spears, who has said she is effectively retired from the music business, has not released a new album since 2016’s Glory and does not appear to be involved in the promotion of the anniversary edition. She did, however, preview the classic Britney pop banger “ She’ll Never Be Me ,” last month, giving fans a listen to the song she co-wrote with Timberlake along with Bradley Daymond (*NSYNC) and Alex Greggs (*NSYNC, Paris Hilton) and which was co-produced by Riprock ‘n’ Alex G.

The resurfaced unreleased songs are the first “new” music from Spears since she teamed with will.i.am on 2023’s one-off “Mind Your Business.” In January, Spears vowed that she would “ never perform in the U.S. again ,” seven years after wrapping her global Piece of Me tour.

entertainment.title: How John Summit Is Turning Arenas Into the “World’s Biggest Nightclub” for CTRL ESCAPE Tour
entertainment.summary: When the 32-year-old DJ pitched his first-ever arena tour to his team, he had one goal: To create a show fans had "never seen before at a scale that no DJ has really done." Now that idea is a reality.
entertainment.body:
“I’m always about doing things first and really breaking the mold and breaking barriers, especially in the DJ world,” John Summit says. That mentality spawned the 32-year-old DJ’s idea to embark on his first-ever arena tour.

For any DJ, organizing a global arena tour is a tall order, as their home away from home is typically nightclubs and music festivals. While Summit has become a fixture in those spaces in recent years, he also saw an opportunity for something bigger.

Following one-off shows at New York’s Madison Square Garden and Los Angeles’ Kia Forum, Summit admits he didn’t even want to flirt with the idea of a full arena run initially because there are a limited number of DJs capable of pulling off a tour on a similar scale to massive mainstream pop acts. Related Stories Music Singer Jackson Wang Signs With WME (Exclusive) Music With 'The Girl of Your Dreams,' Ashe Finds Her Sweet Spot: "I'm A Really Solid Version of Myself"

Sure, a handful of DJs such as The Chainsmokers and Kaskade have launched their own versions of arena and stadium tours. Still, Summit considers his multi-country CTRL ESCAPE Arena Tour a particularly unique and ambitious opportunity, as he’s the sole headliner on each date, and it’s strictly a DJ set rather than mixed in with pop performances.

“There’s been DJs who’ve played arenas, but to this scale and this level, this is a very ambitious tour and it’s not something I technically have to do because obviously the clubs and festivals and everything has been working so well,” Summit tells The Hollywood Reporter . “But because I did those one-off shows and they worked out super well, I knew that I had the confidence to actually take the show on the road.”

Luckily for Summit, the tour’s visual concept came easily as his sophomore album CTRL ESCAPE already had a theme centered around breaking out of the corporate 9-to-5 “matrix.” The notion was personal for Summit, as he left his job as a CPA in 2019 to follow his passion for music — and it clearly worked out.

“The fans can relate as well too because you’re going to that show; they probably all worked their 9-to-5 during the day to then be able to afford the ticket at night,” Summit says. “So it’s going to be that show is their way of breaking out of that.”

It was important for Summit to build a world that his fans could truly escape into, so he leaned on his creative director, Alex Alvga, who also worked on his sophomore album and other shows, to channel the corporate-to-rave transformation that originated in his “LIGHTS GO OUT” music video.

entertainment.title: Romanian First-Ever Country of Focus at AFM, ‘Fjord’ Director Cristian Mungiu to Attend
entertainment.summary: The American Film Market, traditionally known for mainstream commercial cinema, will shine a spotlight on Romanian arthouse movies at this year's event.
entertainment.body:
In a surprise move, the American Film Market , traditional home to mainstream cinema in all its schlocky glory, is going upscale arthouse.

At next week’s AFM — Nov. 10-15 at the Fairmont Century Plaza in Los Angeles — there will be a focus on Romanian cinema. AFM has named Romania its first-ever country of focus. National film industry group Creative Romanian Filmmakers (CRFM) will bring over a delegation of filmmakers, producers and production companies to present their latest movies and to meet with industry execs to discuss shooting in Romanian and international co-production opportunities. Related Stories Movies 'an open field' Is a Deeply Personal Story of Loss, Grief and Compassion (Exclusive Netflix Trailer) Movies 'Elsinore' to Close Camerimage Festival

“Romania has been part of the AFM community for many years, and we’re proud to recognize its contributions to global cinema as our first-ever Country of Focus,” said Jackie Brenneman, President & CEO of the Independent Film & Television Alliance (IFTA), which produces the AFM. “Together with Creative Romanian Filmmakers, we look forward to showcasing the country’s exceptional talent and opportunities for international collaboration.”

“Since 2016, Creative Romanian Filmmakers has brought Romanian producers to the world’s most important film markets and festivals, and the American Film Market has always been a key stop on that journey,” added CRFM managing director Mihai Lupu. “Being named Country of Focus this year is a milestone for our entire industry – an invitation to buyers, sales agents and producers to discover Romanian stories, talent and locations, and to build lasting partnerships with us.”

The delegation will include Cristian Mungiu , attending with his Palme d’Or winning drama Fjord , starring Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve . Fjord is Romania’s official entry for the Oscar in the best international feature category and is seen as a shoo-in for the Academy long-list, being announced Dec. 15.

“This year, a Romanian film was awarded at every major festival,” noted Mungiu. “I believe Romanian films have real potential in international markets – not only at festivals, but with a wider audience. In this sense, Fjord ’s awards-season campaign and its North American theatrical release look promising.”

Mungiu also put in a pitch for his country as a shooting location, noting that “not only is the Romanian cash rebate working again, we have also started a conversation with the Romanian authorities about providing upfront cash-flow financing for the rebate, and we hope to see concrete results as early as 2027.”

entertainment.title: Weezer: Photos From the Billboard Cover Shoot
entertainment.summary: Check out new pics of the legendary alt-rockers ahead of their Billboard Live Music Summit appearance.
entertainment.body:
Rivers Cuomo is reclining in a zero-gravity chair in a musty, windowless room deep within Tampa, Fla.’s Benchmark Arena — baseball cap on his head, a copy of Cormac McCarthy’s Blood Meridian and a pair of headphones beside him. Nearby, there’s a keyboard, a small drum kit and an acoustic guitar that his Weezer bandmate, drummer Patrick Wilson, periodically picks up and noodles on; a jar of peanut butter; a printed, official-looking setlist on a spreadsheet; and a paper bag labeled “clarinet books” in marker.

It’s flummoxing to consider that in just a few hours, this soft-spoken iteration of the Weezer frontman will be channeling the power-pop gods onstage for thousands of screaming fans. But this is Cuomo in power-saving mode, restoring the energy he burned onstage the night prior outside of Fort Lauderdale and didn’t quite recover on the four-hour overnight bus ride across the Sunshine State.

Yet at precisely 9:12 p.m. on this October night — just like every show night this tour — the lights will go down for Weezer’s headlining set, and Cuomo will transform. This is the precise time that, like clockwork, the lights have gone down for every show on the Weezer: The Gathering Tour, and it’s the time they will continue to go down for its remainder; if all goes as planned, Weezer will leave the stage at 10:53 p.m. on the dot.

A prerecorded video plays, setting up the show’s concept: A kid makes a wish for Weezer to play at his house, and when the quartet receives the magical transmission, it links up to answer the call. Finally, after the clip rolls, one of the great American rock bands strides onto the stage — which is decked out with a fake house, fence, yard and power lines to resemble the home from the video.

“Dearly beloved, we’re gathered here tonight,” Cuomo declares into his mic as the band revs up, “to celebrate a thing called Weezer!”

Read the full Weezer Billboard cover story here. Weezer will be honored with the Legend of Live award and sit down for an exclusive Q&A at the 2026 Billboard Live Music Summit on Nov. 10 at the 1 Hotel West Hollywood. Tickets for the Nov. 10 event are available here .

Clockwise from left: Brian Bell, Scott Shriner, Patrick Wilson, and Rivers Cuomo.

entertainment.title: ‘an open field’ Is a Deeply Personal Story of Loss, Grief and Compassion (Exclusive Netflix Trailer)
entertainment.summary: The award-winning short film, directed by Teboho Edkins and produced by his father, dives into the mourning following the death of the filmmaker’s brother in a Boeing airplane crash over Ethiopia.
entertainment.body:
In March 2019, a Boeing 737 MAX crashed in Ethiopia just six minutes after taking off from the airport in the country’s capital, Addis Ababa. It had 157 people on board, and all of them died. Among them was Max Thabiso Edkins . His older brother Teboho Edkins decided to make a film about the experience of grief and mourning that his family and the local community went through. The result is the very personal 38-minute short film an open field , directed by Edkins and produced by his father, Don Edkins, and Carine Chichkowsky. The film is now going global, hitting Netflix on Dec. 1, about a year after its world premiere at the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam ( IDFA ) 2025, where it won the best short documentary award. Related Stories Business Netflix Taps Mattel's Roberto Stanichi to Lead Consumer Products and Experiences Business Dark Slope to Open New Virtual Production Stage in Vancouver (Exclusive)

The title of the movie becomes clear when you watch it. In an open field, the filmmaker finds out that dozens of nearby villagers immediately converged on the crash site to help. Some even stood vigil for a month to protect and preserve the area. Years later, they continue to mourn alongside family members who visit the site, including Edkins and his father, also making the film a story about collective grief and compassion.

“Boeing’s widely criticized response to the crash stands in sharp contrast to the community’s enduring compassion,” highlights a synopsis. “Both a personal essay on loss and an exploration of the potential healing power of collective mourning, Edkins’s film is a quiet testament to humanity – moments of warmth, resolve, grief, fear, patience, and simple acts of kindness.” Indeed, the film feels like a cinematic attempt to connect with a late brother and son’s spirit. In that sense, an open field is a family film. And it may be set in a far-away place for many viewers, but it transcends borders, given that the plane’s passengers came from more than 30 countries and that anyone who has lost a loved one has faced the burden of that loss.

an open field is a South Africa-France-Germany production by Day Zero Film and Video Productions in South Africa, Day Zero Films UG in Germany and Survivance in France. The cinematographer is Jide Akinleminu, the editor is Anne Fabini. The film, shot in color and black-and-white, features dialogue in both English and Amharic.

entertainment.title: ‘Elsinore’ to Close Camerimage Festival
entertainment.summary: Simon Stone’s true-life drama, shot by Mike Eley, stars Andrew Scott as British actor Ian Charleson, who, succumbing to AIDS, throws himself into a final performance of 'Hamlet.'
entertainment.body:
Elsinore , Simon Stone’s award season contender starring Andrew Scott , will close the 34th edition of Camerimage .

The real-life drama, shot by Mike Eley, stars Scott as Ian Charleson, the Scottish actor best known for Chariots of Fire , who in the last days of his life before succumbing to AIDS, threw himself into a final stage performance of Hamlet . Olivia Colman, Joe Locke and Johnny Flynn co-star.

The film, written by Stephen Beresford, premiered at Telluride and opened the BFI London Film Festival in October. Related Stories Movies "The Biggest Role of My Life -- So Far": Breakout Star Reggie Absolom on Putting the 'Kid' in 'Club Kid' Movies For 'Father's House,' Former Cult Members and Lauded Actors Collaborated to Explore Mechanisms of Control in a Cinematic Experiment

The closing-night slot follows a program that brings together a number of this year’s awards contenders . Among the titles in competition for the festival’s Golden Frog trophy are Project Hail Mary , directed by Phil Lord and Christopher Miller and shot by Greig Fraser; Steven Spielberg’s Disclosure Day , with cinematography by Janusz Kamiński; and Martin McDonagh’s Wild Horse Nine , shot by Ben Davis. The competition also includes Tony Gilroy’s Behemoth! , photographed by Damián García; Minotaur , from Russian director Andrey Zvyagintsev and shot by longtime collaborator Mikhail Krichman; and May el-Toukhy’s Venice Film Festival winner Woman Unknown , shot by Jasper J. Spanning.

Other competition entries are Paweł Pawlikowski’s Fatherland , shot by Lukasz Zal; Hans Petter Moland’s Growth of the Soil , photographed by Oskar Dahlsbakken; and Visitation , directed by Volker Schlöndorff and shot by Axel Schneppat.

Camerimage, the largest festival dedicated to the art of cinematography, runs Nov. 7-14.

entertainment.title: Fox Closes Roku Deal, Creating New Streaming Power Player
entertainment.summary: The $22 billion deal closed in less than five months. Roku CEO Anthony Wood will join Fox's board and serve as co-chair of the company's digital division.
entertainment.body:
Fox Corp . has completed its $22 billion acquisition of Roku , creating a new power player in media and streaming.

Roku founder Anthony Wood will join Fox’s board and also serve as co-chair of Fox Digital Platforms, the division that will house Roku, Tubi, Fox One and Red Seat Ventures.

“The closing of this acquisition advances the long-term strategy of Fox,” Fox CEO Lachlan Murdoch said in a statement. “Beginning today, our top priority for the combined company is to continue to relentlessly serve audiences and partners, while reinforcing the openness and choice that is the essence of the Roku platform. Our shared entrepreneurial passion and clear conviction toward building the future together with our new Roku colleagues gives us great confidence in the opportunities ahead of us.”

“We started Roku more than two decades ago to give people a better way to watch TV, and that mission doesn’t change today,” Wood added. “What does change is our reach and resources. Fox has a deep respect for Roku’s culture and wholly shares our commitment to staying open to every content partner. Our teams will keep building and innovating as they always have, now with the support and capabilities of Fox behind us. I’m proud of what Roku’s employees have built, and I’m excited about what comes next.”

The deal makes Fox into a major player in streaming, with two of the largest free streaming video platforms on the market in Tubi and Roku Channel, a premium streaming service in Fox One, and perhaps most importantly an install base of more than 100 million households around the world. It is no exaggeration to say that Roku is the gateway to TV (inclusive of Netflix, YouTube, Disney+ etc) for a significant chunk of the U.S.

The deal closed in less than five months, a fast pace for a deal this size. In September, the U.S. Department of Justice was revealed to be reviewing the deal. It has obviously cleared it since then.

The mega-merger has been more than a year in the making, with Wood telling Roku’s board last fall that he as contemplating stepping back from the company. The end result was a sale process, with Wood agreeing to continue serving as an executive in some capacity for an amount of time to be determined.

entertainment.title: ‘Buena Vista Social Club’ to Close on Broadway in January
entertainment.summary: The show is on track to recoup before closing, and will make a move to London's West End in 2027.
entertainment.body:
Buena Vista Social Club will play its final performance Jan. 17 after close to two years on Broadway .

The musical, inspired by the titular Cuban band, took home five Tony Awards in 2025, including a special Tony for its onstage band. While the show is closing in January, producers say it is on track to recoup before closure, making it the second musical of the 2024-2025 to announce recoupment.

The show also has a touring production, and currently has productions in Puerto Rico and Mexico City. In 2027, the musical will open in London’s West End.

Buena Vista Social Club is the first show on Broadway to feature a score sung entirely in Spanish. The story is based on the creation of the Buena Vista Social Club’s 1997 album, which was made up of legends in the 1950s Cuban music scene and toggles between the creation of the album and the past.

The musical opened on March 19, 2025, at the Gerald Schoenfeld Theatre, after starting previews in February 2025. The musical is still commanding high attendance, though its grosses have gradually fallen from the highs of 2025. It is the second musical of its season to recoup, following Just In Time , which is still running.

The show features a book by Marco Ramirez, direction by Saheem Ali and choreography by Patricia Delgado and Justin Peck. Lead producer Orin Wolf also hinted at a possible film deal.

“From our very first trip to Cuba to meet the musicians who created this masterpiece, I knew we had something truly special, something to cherish. I am in awe of what Marco R., Saheem, Patricia, Justin, David, Marco P. and Dean have created artistically, bringing this extraordinary music to life on stage and presenting the first Broadway score performed exclusively in Spanish,” said Wolf. “I am deeply grateful for the time we’ve had on Broadway – and the speed with which the team has created three more productions. We are thrilled the Broadway production is on schedule to recoup as we look ahead to an exciting tour, special engagements in Mexico and Puerto Rico, the film and so much more.”

In addition to the onstage band, the cast of Buena Vista Social Club currently includes Gina Torres (Omara), Rick Negron (Compay), Mel Semé (Ibrahim), Jainardo Batista Sterling (Rubén), Isa Antonetti (Young Omara), Da’Von T. Moody (Young Compay), Wesley Wray (Young Ibrahim), Jesús Pupo (Young Rubén), Renesito Avich (Eliades), Tanairi Sade Vazquez (Young Haydee), Chris Myers (Juan de Marcos) and José “Candelita” Iglesias (The Narrator).
